summary: SpaceX's global headquarters sits on Crenshaw Boulevard in Hawthorne, making this 6.1-square-mile city one of the most improbable aerospace hubs in the country — a flat, densely packed grid of residential blocks and commercial strips that also houses a rocket factory. That juxtaposition defines the place: a median home value of $813,700 against a median household income of $72,719 yields a price-to-income ratio above 11, meaning ownership is out of reach at the median without substantial outside capital or dual high incomes. Renting at $1,723 per month is more plausible but still absorbs nearly 30% of gross median income. The terrain is pancake-flat coastal plain, just three miles from the ocean, which delivers that mild 73°F average high and 9.2 hours of daily sunshine year-round — genuinely temperate weather with almost no seasonal drama. The street grid is functional but fragmented by wide arterials like Hawthorne Boulevard and the 105 freeway cutting through, which chops the city into sections that don't always connect gracefully on foot. Beyond SpaceX, proximity to LAX and the broader South Bay defense-and-logistics corridor means employment options exist without a brutal commute, though the 405 remains the 405. At its core, Hawthorne is a working aerospace city wearing the price tag of coastal Los Angeles County, and that tension between blue-collar bones and seven-figure housing is the defining math of daily life here.
